Lerøy Havfisk's catch volume fell to 64 991 tonnes (HOG) in 2024, a substantial decrease from 75 893 tonnes in 2023 [1]. The fall reflects quota cuts of 34% for cod, 43% for haddock, and 6% for saithe in the northern zone [1][2]. The quota reduction is partly offset by higher prices, which help the trawler fleet but challenge the land-based industry [2]. Onshore whitefish processing made another loss in 2024, larger than 2023's despite improved KPIs like yield [2]. 1st edition (1859) - assumptions: breeds when thirty years old, goes on breeding till ninety years old, bringing forth three pair of young in this interval
1st edition (1859) - result: at the end of the fifth century there would be alive fifteen million elephants, descended from the first pair
6th edition (1872) - assumptions: begins breeding when thirty years old, goes on breeding till ninety years old, bringing forth six young in the interval, and surviving till one hundred years old
6th edition (1872) - result: after a period of from 740 to 750 years there would be nearly nineteen million elephants alive descended from the first pair

Between editions, Darwin changed the young from "three pair" to "six young" and added the assumption that elephants survive till one hundred years old; the result changed from fifteen million elephants at the end of the fifth century to nearly nineteen million elephants after 740 to 750 years.

It persists among the wealthy classes of countries with a lower, more archaic industrial structure, and among recent accessions to wealth in advanced communities who have not yet shed the plebeian canons of taste from their former lower pecuniary grade—for example, higher social classes in American cities that have recently and rapidly risen into opulence (Chapter Seven, [3]).

More broadly, it continues wherever and so long as it serves as evidence of honorific leisure by arguing physical disability in the wearer, persisting through the period of "snobbery"—the transition from a lower to an upper level of pecuniary culture (Chapter Seven, [4]).

Darwin calls it Malthus's doctrine applied to the animal and vegetable kingdoms [1]. In Malthus's essay, population when unchecked increases in a geometrical ratio, while subsistence increases only in an arithmetical ratio [3]. He takes as his rule, based on the United States experience, that unchecked population doubles itself every twenty-five years [2].

Mill sees the deeper danger in social tyranny over thought and the soul, while Tocqueville sees it in the majority's omnipotence leaving the individual no means of escape or redress.
